page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage, meaning storage must be provisioned externally.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in several areas. The AMD EPYC CPU achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as PassMark CPU and physics evaluations. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by AVX-512 and SHA-NI instruction sets. Memory bandwidth tests place the system in the top 25% for both cached and uncached read/write operations, though the overall PassMark memory score falls into the average category. For data processing, the server registers top 10% results in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and bzip3 decompression.

The dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs support machine learning tasks. LLM inference benchmarks demonstrate top 10% performance for small 135M models and top 25% for medium 7B models, though performance drops to average levels for large 70B models. The shared CPU allocation and lack of integrated local storage represent architectural tradeoffs that require external storage attachments and may introduce resource contention. This configuration is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, medium-scale LLM inference, image processing, and database operations.
